issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (North America)

plan.diagnosis: Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC represents $1,057,835 in annual spend with dependency on 33 sub-tier suppliers, including a single-source sub-tier in North America that has experienced 2 disruption events in the past 12 months. Despite a relatively strong resiliency score of 81, the single-source sub-tier dependency creates medium-severity supply chain concentration risk valued at $1,057,835.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping exercise with Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC to identify the single-source North America sub-tier supplier, document criticality, and assess the impact of the 2 recent disruption events

Issue RFI to qualify 2-3 alternate sub-tier suppliers in North America capable of supporting Shenzhen Hua Pacific's requirements, targeting suppliers with disruption history of 0 events over 12 months
Negotiate contractual terms with Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC requiring dual-source commitment at sub-tier level with 60-day buffer inventory for critical components
Establish quarterly sub-tier risk reviews with Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC and implement early warning system for disruption events across all 33 sub-tier suppliers
Develop contingency plan including pre-qualified backup suppliers and emergency sourcing protocols to mitigate future single-source sub-tier exposure across the $1,057,835 spend

plan.expected_impact: Mitigating single-source sub-tier risk will protect $1,057,835 in annual spend and reduce disruption probability by establishing dual-source sub-tier coverage, targeting 50% reduction in supply chain exposure or approximately $528,918 in protected spend value.
kpis: Number of qualified alternate sub-tier suppliers (target: minimum 1 alternate)
Sub-tier supplier disruption events per quarter (baseline: 2 over 12 months, target: <1 per quarter)
Percentage of spend covered by dual-source sub-tier arrangement (target: 100% of $1,057,835)
Sub-tier transparency score (percentage of 33 sub-tier suppliers mapped and monitored, target: 100%)
Average lead time buffer inventory at sub-tier level (target: 60 days for critical items)
risks: Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC may resist sub-tier transparency due to proprietary supplier relationships
Limited alternate sub-tier suppliers in North America market may extend qualification timeline beyond 4 weeks
Dual-sourcing requirements may increase costs by 5-10% on $1,057,835 spend base ($52,892-$105,784)
The 2 disruption events in past 12 months may recur during transition period before alternates are qualified
Cross-ERP visibility challenges (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) may delay sub-tier spend analysis and monitoring
erp_actions: SAP: Create new info record (ME11) flagging Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC (vendor master LFA1) with sub-tier risk indicator and mandatory source approval workflow in ME01
SAP: Update vendor master (XK02) with enhanced monitoring flag in LFA1-SPERR field and add risk notes in LFA1-TXTMD documentation
Coupa: Tag supplier profile for Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC with 'SUB_TIER_RISK' attribute and set approval threshold at $50,000 for additional oversight
Oracle EBS: Add supplier site attribute 'SUBTIER_SINGLE_SOURCE' and configure hold on POs >$100,000 pending sub-tier validation in PO Headers
NetSuite: Create custom field on vendor record for sub-tier supplier count (value: 33) and disruption event counter (value: 2) with quarterly review reminder workflow
Dynamics 365: Enable advanced procurement policy requiring sub-tier mapping document attachment for all POs to Shenzhen Hua Pacific Services LLC
Multi-ERP: Establish centralized vendor risk dashboard consolidating spend data ($1,057,835) and sub-tier metrics across all 5 ERP systems with weekly refresh
